It operates on the todo_list_todos table from the Prisma schema and returns the complete todo entity including all fields such as title, description, priority, due date, completion status, creation timestamp, and last update timestamp. The operation enforces data ownership rules to ensure users can only access their own todo items.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo item
operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive details for a single todo item specified by its unique identifier.

This operation provides access to the complete todo entity with all available fields and metadata. It serves the use case where users need to view full details of a specific task, including the complete description, priority level, due date information, completion status, and timestamps for creation and last modification.

The operation implements strict ownership verification to ensure users can only retrieve their own todo items. The system validates that the authenticated user (identified by the JWT token) is the owner of the requested todo item. If a user attempts to access a todo belonging to another user, the operation returns an authorization error, maintaining data privacy and security.

This endpoint is typically used when users click on a todo item from their list to view or edit its details, or when the application needs to refresh the current state of a specific todo item. The response includes all todo fields as defined in the Prisma schema, providing a complete representation of the task entity.

Security considerations include proper authorization checks to prevent unauthorized access, validation of the todo ID format to ensure it's a valid UUID, and protection against enumeration attacks through consistent error responses for both non-existent and unauthorized todo items.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item in the user's todo list. It operates on the todo_list_todos table from the Prisma schema, allowing authenticated users to add new tasks to their personal todo collection. The operation accepts todo item details including title, description, priority, due date, and completion status, then persists the new todo item to the database with the authenticated user's ID as the owner.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item for the authenticated user
operations.description:
Create a new todo item in the authenticated user's personal todo list.

This operation allows users to add new tasks to their todo collection by providing essential task information such as title, description, priority level, due date, and initial completion status. The system automatically associates the created todo item with the authenticated user through their user ID extracted from the JWT token.

Security: Only authenticated users can create todo items. The user_id field is automatically populated from the authentication token, ensuring users can only create todos under their own account. Rate limiting applies to prevent spam todo creation.

The created todo item becomes immediately available in the user's todo list and can be retrieved through list or detail operations. Users can subsequently update or delete the todo item as needed.

Related operations: Update todo (PUT /todos/{todoId}), List todos (PATCH /todos), Get todo detail (GET /todos/{todoId}).

requestBody.description: Todo item creation data including title, description, priority, due date, and completion status

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all fields including system-generated ID and timestamps

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item in the user's todo list. It operates on the todo_list_todos table from the Prisma schema, allowing authenticated users to modify their existing tasks. The operation accepts the todo item's unique identifier in the path and update data in the request body, then persists the modifications to the database while enforcing ownership validation to ensure users can only update their own todos.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item in the authenticated user's personal todo list.

This operation allows users to modify their existing tasks by providing updated information for fields such as title, description, priority level, due date, and completion status. The system validates that the todo item exists and belongs to the authenticated user before applying any modifications.

Security: Only authenticated users can update todo items, and users can only update todos they own. The system performs ownership verification by comparing the todo item's user_id with the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token. Attempting to update another user's todo will result in an authorization error.

The updated todo item is immediately reflected in the user's todo list. All provided fields in the request body will overwrite the existing values, while omitted optional fields retain their current values. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp upon successful modification.

Validation: The operation validates that the todoId exists in the database and that all provided update values meet the schema constraints defined in the todo_list_todos table.

Related operations: Create todo (POST /todos), List todos (PATCH /todos), Get todo detail (GET /todos/{todoId}), Delete todo (DELETE /todos/{todoId}).

It operates on the todo_list_todos table and performs a hard delete, completely removing the record. The operation requires the todo's unique identifier and validates ownership to ensure users can only delete their own todos.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a specific todo item
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item from the user's task list. This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the todo record from the database without any possibility of recovery.

The operation validates that the authenticated user owns the todo item before allowing deletion. This ensures data privacy and prevents unauthorized deletion of other users' tasks. If the todo does not exist or belongs to a different user, the operation will fail with an appropriate error.

Security: Only authenticated users can delete todos, and they can only delete their own items. The user's identity is extracted from the JWT authentication token. This operation is irreversible - once a todo is deleted, it cannot be recovered. Consider implementing a completion status instead of deletion for tasks that should be preserved in history.

Related operations: Mark todo as complete (PUT /todos/{todoId}), Create new todo (POST /todos), List todos (PATCH /todos).

It computes metrics such as total todo count, completed count, pending count, completion rate, and other derived analytics. This is a computed operation that does not map to a single Prisma table but aggregates data from the todo_list_todos table using GROUP BY and COUNT operations.
operations.summary: Retrieve aggregated statistics about user's todo items
operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive statistical metrics about the authenticated user's todo items. This operation provides analytical insights into task management patterns including completion rates, pending tasks, and overall productivity metrics.

The statistics are computed in real-time by aggregating data from the user's todo collection. Metrics include total number of todos created, number of completed todos, number of pending/incomplete todos, completion percentage rate, and potentially time-based trends if additional filtering is applied.

Security: Only authenticated users can access statistics, and the data is automatically filtered to include only the requesting user's todos. The user's identity is extracted from the JWT authentication token, ensuring complete data privacy and isolation between users.

This operation serves dashboard and overview requirements, providing users with at-a-glance insights into their task management effectiveness. The computed metrics help users understand their productivity patterns and task completion behavior.

Implementation note: This operation executes aggregation queries (COUNT, SUM, AVG) on the todo_list_todos table filtered by the authenticated user's ID. The response is a computed DTO containing statistical summaries rather than direct table rows.

responseBody.description: Statistical metrics and aggregated data about user's todo items

current.description:
Current page number in the paginated result set.

Represents the zero-based or one-based index of the current page being returned in the response. This value indicates which page of results the client is currently viewing.

This field is used by clients to track their position in the paginated data set and to construct subsequent page requests. The value should match the page number requested by the client in their original query.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records returned per page.

Defines the page size limit that was applied when retrieving this paginated result set. This value determines how many records are included in a single page response.

Clients use this value in combination with the current page number to calculate offset positions and to understand how results are chunked. The actual number of records in the response may be less than this limit on the final page.

records.description:
Total number of records available in the database matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete count of all records that satisfy the search or filter conditions, regardless of pagination. This is the total across all pages, not just the current page.

Clients use this value to calculate total page counts, display result statistics to users, and determine whether additional pages exist. This value remains constant across all pages of the same query unless the underlying data changes.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available for the current query.

Calculated by dividing the total records by the page limit and applying ceiling rounding: Math.ceil(records / limit). This represents how many pages are required to display all matching records.

Clients use this value to render pagination controls, determine if next/previous page buttons should be enabled, and validate page number inputs. A value of 0 indicates no results were found.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata structure returned with paginated API responses.

This schema defines the standard pagination information object that accompanies paginated list responses across all API endpoints. It provides clients with essential metadata needed to navigate through large result sets efficiently.

The pagination object enables clients to understand their current position in the result set, calculate total pages, render pagination UI components, and construct requests for subsequent or previous pages. All numeric values use zero-based or one-based indexing consistently throughout the API.

This structure is typically embedded within response objects under a 'pagination' or 'data' wrapper, alongside the actual array of result items.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the user session listing response.

Provides comprehensive pagination information including the current page number, page size limit, total number of session records matching the query criteria, and the total number of pages available. This metadata enables clients to render pagination controls, navigate between pages, and display result statistics to users.

The pagination object follows the standard IPage.IPagination schema structure used consistently across all paginated endpoints in the API. Clients use these values to construct subsequent page requests by adjusting the page parameter in their queries.

Essential for user interfaces that display session listings with navigation controls, allowing users to browse through potentially large collections of active authentication sessions across multiple devices and time periods.

data.description:
Array of user session summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual session data retrieved from the todo_list_user_sessions table, with each element representing an active or expired authentication session. Each session summary includes essential information such as session ID, user reference, IP address, connection URLs (href and referrer), creation timestamp, and expiration status.

The number of elements in this array will be less than or equal to the pagination.limit value, with the final page potentially containing fewer records than the limit. An empty array indicates no sessions match the current filter criteria for this page.

Each session record provides sufficient information for security monitoring displays, enabling users to identify active sessions across different devices and locations, monitor session age, and detect suspicious login patterns. The summary variant is optimized for list views while excluding detailed authentication token information.

IPageITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Paginated response containing a collection of user session summaries.

This schema defines the standard paginated response structure for user session listing operations. It wraps an array of session summary records with pagination metadata, enabling efficient browsing of potentially large session collections through controlled page-based data retrieval.

The response combines session data from the todo_list_user_sessions table with pagination information following the standard IPage pattern used throughout the API. This structure supports both user self-service session management (viewing own active sessions across devices) and administrative security monitoring (reviewing user sessions for support and security purposes).

Used as the response body for PATCH operations on session listing endpoints, where the request body contains search filters and pagination parameters. The pagination wrapper enables clients to navigate through results, display page controls, and show total result counts to users. Each page contains up to the specified limit of session records, with the data array potentially empty when no sessions match the filter criteria or when requesting a page beyond the available data range.

This paginated structure is essential for scalable session management interfaces that need to handle users with multiple concurrent sessions across different devices and time periods.

IPageITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:

The pagination wrapper provides essential navigation information including current page number, total record count, page size limits, and total page count. This enables client applications to implement pagination controls for navigating through admin session history.

Typically returned by administrator session listing operations that support filtering by creation date, IP address, session status, or other security-relevant criteria. Critical for security auditing workflows where administrators need to review and monitor authentication patterns across the administrative user base.

IPageITodoListEmailVerification.ISummary.description:

This response type wraps a list of email verification records with pagination metadata, enabling efficient navigation through verification history for user accounts. Used in user account management interfaces and administrative verification monitoring endpoints.

The pagination wrapper provides essential navigation information including current page number, total record count, page size limits, and total page count. This enables client applications to implement pagination controls for browsing through verification attempts and tracking verification completion status.

Typically returned by email verification listing operations that support filtering by verification status, expiration state, creation date, or email address patterns. Essential for user account activation workflows where users or administrators need to review pending verifications, identify expired tokens, or audit verification completion history.

Used as the response type for password reset search operations, providing both the requested data and the information needed to navigate through multiple pages of results. The data array contains ITodoListPasswordReset.ISummary objects with essential reset token information, while the pagination object tracks current page, total records, and total pages.

Array of ITodoListGuest.ISummary objects representing unauthenticated visitors that match the search criteria. Each summary contains essential tracking information including guest identifier, IP address, and visit timestamp.

IPageITodoListGuest.ISummary.description:

IPageITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:

This response type wraps a filtered and sorted list of administrator accounts from the todo_list_admins table with pagination metadata. It represents the result of search and filter operations on administrator data, providing both the matching administrator records and information needed to navigate through multiple pages of results.

The pagination wrapper enables efficient handling of large administrator datasets by dividing results into manageable pages. Each page contains a subset of administrator summary records along with metadata indicating the current page position, total record count, and available pages.

Used as the response type for administrative search operations where administrators query and browse the system's administrator accounts. The summary records contain essential administrator information optimized for list displays, excluding sensitive fields like password hashes.

This structure supports administrative dashboards, user management interfaces, and audit operations where administrators need to view, search, and manage other administrator accounts with proper pagination controls.

IPageITodoListUser.ISummary.description:

This response type wraps a filtered and sorted list of user accounts from the todo_list_users table with pagination metadata. It represents the result of search and filter operations on user data, providing both the matching user records and information needed to navigate through multiple pages of results.

The pagination wrapper enables efficient handling of potentially large user datasets by dividing results into manageable pages. Each page contains a subset of user summary records along with metadata indicating the current page position, total record count, and available pages for navigation.

Used as the response type for administrative user search operations where administrators query and browse registered user accounts. The summary records contain essential user information optimized for list displays while excluding sensitive fields like password hashes, tokens, and detailed session information.

This structure supports administrative dashboards, user management interfaces, analytics views, and account monitoring operations where administrators need to view, search, filter, and analyze user accounts with proper pagination controls and performance optimization.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the todo list response.

Provides comprehensive pagination information including current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count. This enables clients to implement proper pagination controls and display accurate page navigation UI.

The pagination object follows the standard IPage.IPagination structure used throughout the API for consistent pagination handling across all list endpoints. Clients can use this information to calculate page ranges, determine if next/previous pages exist, and display "showing X-Y of Z" indicators.

All pagination calculations account for the user's total accessible todos, which are automatically scoped to only the authenticated user's todo items for privacy and data ownership compliance.

data.description:
Array of todo items for the current page in summary format.

Contains the actual todo records matching the search and filter criteria specified in the request. Each todo is represented in summary format (ITodoListTodo.ISummary) which includes essential fields optimized for list display: id, title, completion status, and creation timestamp.

The number of items in this array is controlled by the limit parameter in the request (maximum 100 items per page). The specific items returned depend on the page number, applied filters (completion status, priority, due date ranges), search terms, and sort order.

All todos in this array belong exclusively to the authenticated user, as enforced by automatic user_id scoping in the backend. This ensures complete data isolation and privacy between different users' todo lists.

IPageITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Paginated response containing a list of todo items with metadata for the authenticated user.

This schema represents the complete response structure returned by the todo list retrieval endpoint (PATCH /todoList/user/todos). It combines the actual todo data with pagination information to enable efficient browsing of potentially large todo lists.

The response is structured as a standard paginated collection following the IPage pattern used throughout the API. This consistency enables clients to implement reusable pagination components across different list views.

All data is automatically scoped to the authenticated user based on their JWT token, ensuring complete privacy and data ownership. The todo items are sourced from the todo_list_todos Prisma table with automatic filtering by the user's todo_list_user_id.

This schema is used exclusively for search and list operations where users need to browse, filter, and navigate through their todo collections. The summary format of individual todos is optimized for list rendering performance, excluding verbose fields like full descriptions while retaining essential information for task identification and status display.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This field captures the network address from which the guest registration request originates. While optional, providing the IP address enables better security monitoring, fraud detection, and session management.

The IP address can be IPv4 or IPv6 format. The server may also extract this from request headers, but clients can provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios or when using proxy configurations.

This information is stored in the todo_list_guests table and associated session records for audit trail purposes and to help identify suspicious activities or multiple registrations from the same source.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the current page from which the guest registration was initiated.

This field captures the full URL of the page where the user triggered the guest registration action. It provides context about the user's journey and entry point into the application.

The href is essential for analytics, tracking user acquisition sources, and understanding which parts of the application drive guest registrations. It helps identify effective landing pages and user flows.

This value is stored in the session record and can be used for debugging session-related issues and improving user experience based on registration context.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page the user visited before the guest registration page.

This field captures where the user came from before initiating guest registration. It can be an external website, a search engine, or another page within the application.

The referrer information is valuable for understanding user acquisition channels, marketing campaign effectiveness, and navigation patterns. It helps track whether users are coming from organic search, paid advertising, social media, or direct navigation.

For direct access (user typed URL or used bookmark), this field can be an empty string. This is stored in the session record for analytics and user behavior analysis.

ITodoListGuest.ICreate.description:
Guest account creation request containing session context information.

This schema defines the data required to register a new guest account in the Todo list application. Guest accounts provide temporary, limited access to the service without requiring full user registration.

The schema includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that are essential for establishing the guest's initial session. These fields enable proper audit trails, security monitoring, and analytics tracking.

Since guest registration is a self-signup operation (the guest themselves is creating their own account), the session context fields are included to populate the todo_list_guest_sessions table immediately upon account creation.

Guest accounts have restricted permissions and cannot create or manage todo items, but they can explore the service interface and view public information. This provides a low-friction entry point for users who want to experience the service before committing to full registration.

The IP address is optional as the server can extract it from request headers, but href and referrer are required as the client must provide these values explicitly for accurate session tracking.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated guest account.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key in the todo_list_guests table and uniquely identifies the guest user throughout their session.

ip.description:
IP address of the guest visitor.

Captures the network address from which the visitor accessed the application. This information is essential for security monitoring, geographic analytics, and fraud prevention.

IP addresses are handled in accordance with privacy policies and data protection regulations. They may be used for rate limiting, abuse prevention, and legitimate security purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest visitor record was first created.

Indicates the exact moment when the visitor first accessed the application. This timestamp is automatically set by the system and is immutable.

Used for analyzing visit patterns, calculating session durations, and tracking visitor conversion timelines.

ITodoListGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response for guest accounts with JWT tokens.

This schema represents the complete authentication information returned after successful guest registration or token refresh. It follows the standard authorization response pattern used across the application.

The response includes the guest's unique identifier and a complete token pair (access token and refresh token) that enables the guest to access protected endpoints and maintain their session through token refresh mechanisms.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token issued during guest registration.

This token is used to obtain a new access token without requiring re-registration. The refresh token must be currently valid and not expired, and it must be associated with an active guest account in the todo_list_guests table.

The token is validated against stored refresh token records and session data to ensure authenticity and prevent unauthorized token reuse.

ITodoListGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing guest JWT access tokens.

This schema defines the data required to renew a guest user's access token using their existing refresh token. The operation enables continuous guest sessions by allowing token renewal without requiring users to re-register.

Used in the guest token refresh flow where short-lived access tokens can be renewed using long-lived refresh tokens, maintaining security while providing seamless user experience.

email.description:
User's email address for account creation and authentication.

Must be unique across all users in the todo_list_users table. The email is validated against RFC 5322 email format standards and serves as the primary login credential and user identifier.

This email will be used for authentication, account recovery, and system notifications.

password.description:
User's password for account security.

Provided in plain text during registration and will be securely hashed by the backend before storage in the database. The password should meet minimum security requirements (typically 8+ characters with mixed character types).

The plain text password is never stored; only the hashed version is persisted in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

ip.description:
Client IP address for initial session tracking.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios, or extracted automatically by the server from the request headers. Used for creating the initial session record in todo_list_user_sessions and for security audit purposes.

Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 address formats.

href.description:
Current page URL where the registration request originated.

Required connection metadata indicating the client's current location during account creation. Used for initial session context tracking and security monitoring.

Must be a valid URI format. This metadata is stored in the initial session record created alongside the user account.

referrer.description:
Previous page URL that led to the registration page.

Required connection metadata indicating where the user navigated from before signing up. Used for analytics, tracking user acquisition sources, and understanding registration conversion paths.

Must be a valid URI format. Can be an empty string for direct access cases where there is no previous page.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
User registration data for creating a new account.

Contains all necessary information for creating a new user account in the todo_list_users table and establishing the initial authentication session. This request type is used in the user registration workflow to create the account and issue initial JWT tokens.

The email and password fields are the core credentials required for account creation. The email serves as both the authentication credential and the primary user identifier, and must be unique in the system. The password will be securely hashed before storage.

The ip, href, and referrer fields provide connection context metadata that is used to create the initial session record in the todo_list_user_sessions table. This session is automatically created during registration to enable immediate authentication without requiring a separate login step.

Security considerations: The password is transmitted in plain text but must be sent over HTTPS. The backend will hash the password using industry-standard algorithms before storing it in the password_hash field. The plain text password is never persisted.

Session context fields enable comprehensive tracking of user registration sources and initial session establishment. The href and referrer fields are mandatory as they provide essential context that cannot be reliably inferred server-side, while the ip address is optional since it can be extracted from request headers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user from the todo_list_users table.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the user account and is used for all relational references throughout the system. The identifier is automatically generated upon account creation and remains immutable throughout the user's lifecycle.

This field corresponds to the id primary key column in the todo_list_users Prisma schema.

email.description:
The user's email address used for authentication and communication.

This email serves as the primary login credential and user identifier. It must be unique across all user accounts and is validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

Corresponds to the email column in the todo_list_users table, which has a unique index constraint enforcing email uniqueness.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created.

Automatically set by the system upon account registration during the join operation. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This field is immutable and used for audit trails and account age calculations.

Provides historical context for user lifecycle management and analytics. Corresponds to the created_at column in the todo_list_users Prisma schema.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account information was last modified.

Automatically updated by the system whenever any user account data is changed, including profile updates, password changes, or email verification status changes. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

Used for tracking account activity, audit trails, and synchronization purposes. Corresponds to the updated_at column in the todo_list_users Prisma schema.

email_verified.description:
Whether the user has verified their email address.

Indicates the email verification status based on the email verification process. Users must verify their email address through the verification token system (todo_list_email_verifications table) before accessing certain application features.

This field corresponds to the email_verified boolean column in the todo_list_users Prisma schema. When false, the user may have restricted access until email verification is completed.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the user account was marked as deleted.

When set to a datetime value, indicates the user account has been soft-deleted but preserved in the database for audit purposes and referential integrity. When null, the account is active and not deleted.

Soft-deleted accounts may be excluded from normal queries and prevented from logging in, while maintaining historical data and relationships. Stored in ISO 8601 format when present.

Corresponds to the nullable deleted_at column in the todo_list_users Prisma schema, enabling soft-delete functionality.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response body containing authentication credentials and user profile information after successful authentication.

This interface represents the complete authentication state returned to the user after successful login, registration, or token refresh operations. It includes JWT tokens for maintaining the authenticated session, along with essential user profile information from the todo_list_users table.

The response provides both access and refresh tokens through the IAuthorizationToken structure, enabling the client to store these credentials for subsequent authenticated requests and future token refresh operations.

All user account fields reflect the current state from the todo_list_users Prisma schema, including timestamps, verification status, and soft-delete state. This comprehensive view allows the client to understand the user's account status and handle any necessary UI adjustments based on verification or deletion state.

The email field serves as the primary user identifier in the system, as the todo_list_users table does not include a separate username field.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication.

Must match an existing email in the todo_list_users table. The email is case-insensitive for login purposes and validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

This serves as the username credential for the authentication process.

password.description:
User's password for authentication verification.

Provided in plain text for verification against the securely hashed password stored in the database. The password is transmitted over HTTPS and immediately hashed for comparison without being stored in plain text.

Password should meet minimum security requirements (typically 8+ characters with mixed character types).

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios, or extracted automatically by the server from the request headers. Used for session management, security audit logs, and detecting suspicious login patterns.

Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 address formats.

href.description:
Current page URL where the login request originated.

Required connection metadata indicating the client's current location. Used for session context tracking, security monitoring, and redirect handling after authentication.

Must be a valid URI format. This helps track user navigation patterns and provides context for the authentication event.

referrer.description:
Previous page URL that led to the login page.

Required connection metadata indicating where the user navigated from before reaching the login screen. Used for analytics, tracking user journey, and understanding application entry points.

Must be a valid URI format. Can be an empty string for direct access cases where there is no previous page.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
User login credentials for authentication.

Contains the necessary information for authenticating an existing user and establishing a new session. This request type is used in the user login workflow to validate credentials and issue JWT tokens.

The email and password fields are required for credential validation. The ip, href, and referrer fields provide connection context metadata that is stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table for session tracking and security purposes.

Security considerations: The password is transmitted in plain text but must be sent over HTTPS to ensure encryption in transit. The server will hash the password and compare it against the stored hash without ever storing the plain text password.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) enable the backend to maintain detailed session records for security monitoring, user analytics, and session management. The href and referrer fields are mandatory as they cannot be reliably inferred by the server, while the ip address is optional since the server can extract it from request headers.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token obtained during initial authentication. This token is used to generate new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter their credentials. The refresh token is validated against active session records in the todo_list_user_sessions table to ensure it is still valid and has not been revoked.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This interface defines the data required to refresh authentication tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate. The refresh token provided must be a valid, non-expired token associated with an active user session in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

The refresh token acts as a long-lived credential that can be used to obtain new short-lived access tokens, enabling seamless user experience while maintaining security through token rotation practices.

token.description:
Email verification token received via email during user registration.

This token is generated when a user creates an account and stored in the todo_list_email_verifications table. The token is sent to the user's email address as part of a verification link.

The token must be a valid, non-expired verification token that exists in the database and has not been previously used. Token validation includes checking authenticity, expiration time, and usage status.

Security note: The token should be cryptographically secure and difficult to guess. The system enforces one-time use to prevent token reuse attacks.

ITodoListEmailVerification.IVerify.description:
Request body for email verification endpoint.

Contains the verification token that users submit to verify their email address. This is typically received as a query parameter in an email verification link or submitted through a verification form.

The token is validated against the todo_list_email_verifications table to ensure it is authentic, not expired, and has not been used previously. Successful verification results in the corresponding user account being marked as email-verified in the todo_list_users table.

success.description:
Indicates whether the email verification was successful.

When true, the verification token was valid, not expired, not previously used, and the corresponding user account in the todo_list_users table has been successfully updated to mark the email as verified.

When false, the verification failed due to invalid token, expired token, already-used token, or other validation errors.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the verification result.

Provides detailed feedback about the verification outcome, such as 'Email successfully verified', 'Verification token has expired', 'Invalid verification token', or 'Verification token already used'.

This message helps users understand what happened during the verification process and guides them on next steps if verification failed.

userId.description:
Unique identifier of the user account whose email was verified.

References the id field from the todo_list_users table in the Prisma schema. This field is included in successful verification responses to allow the client to identify which user account was verified.

This can be used by the client application to automatically log in the user or redirect them to their account dashboard after successful email verification.

ITodoListEmailVerification.IResult.description:
Response object returned after email verification attempt.

This type represents the result of validating an email verification token from the todo_list_email_verifications table. It provides comprehensive feedback about whether the verification succeeded or failed, along with contextual information to guide the user experience.

The verification process validates the token against records in todo_list_email_verifications, checking for token authenticity, expiration status, and prior usage. Upon successful validation, the user record in todo_list_users is updated to mark the email as verified.

This response type is used by the email verification endpoint to communicate the outcome of the verification workflow to clients.

email.description:
Email address of the user for password reset or filtering.

For password reset initiation (POST /auth/user/password/reset/request), this email is required and is used to identify the user account in the todo_list_users table and determine where to send the password reset token. The system validates that this is a properly formatted email address but does not reveal in the response whether this email exists in the database (security measure against email enumeration attacks).

For search operations (PATCH endpoints), this field is optional and serves as a filter to retrieve password reset requests for a specific email address.

If the email exists in the system during reset initiation, a password reset token is generated and stored in the todo_list_password_resets table, and reset instructions containing the token are sent to this email address.

page.description:
Page number for pagination in search operations.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when searching password reset requests. Page numbering starts at 1.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

When combined with limit, enables efficient pagination through large result sets. For example, page=2 with limit=20 retrieves records 21-40.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page for pagination.

Controls how many password reset request records are returned in a single response during search operations. Valid range is 1-100 records per page.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Lower limits reduce response size and improve performance, while higher limits reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all data. The 100-record maximum prevents excessive server load.

used.description:
Filter by token usage status in search operations.

When set to true, returns only password reset tokens that have been used to successfully reset a password. When set to false, returns only unused tokens that are still valid for password reset.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Filtering by usage status helps identify active vs consumed tokens, which is useful for security monitoring and determining if a user has multiple pending reset requests.

created_after.description:
Filter for password reset requests created after this timestamp.

Returns only tokens with created_at timestamp later than the specified date-time. Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Useful for finding recent password reset requests or analyzing reset patterns within specific time windows. Commonly combined with created_before to define a time range.

created_before.description:
Filter for password reset requests created before this timestamp.

Returns only tokens with created_at timestamp earlier than the specified date-time. Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Useful for finding historical password reset requests or analyzing reset patterns within specific time windows. Commonly combined with created_after to define a time range.

expires_after.description:
Filter for password reset tokens expiring after this timestamp.

Returns only tokens with expires_at timestamp later than the specified date-time. Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Useful for identifying tokens that are still valid or will remain valid beyond a certain point in time. Helps in monitoring token lifecycle and identifying expired vs active reset opportunities.

expires_before.description:
Filter for password reset tokens expiring before this timestamp.

Returns only tokens with expires_at timestamp earlier than the specified date-time. Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This field is used only in search operations (PATCH endpoints) and is ignored during password reset initiation (POST endpoint).

Useful for identifying expired tokens or tokens that will expire soon, enabling cleanup operations or security monitoring of token expiration patterns.

ITodoListPasswordReset.IRequest.description:
Request body for password reset operations supporting both initiation and search use cases.

This dual-purpose type serves two distinct operation patterns:

**Password Reset Initiation (POST /auth/user/password/reset/request)**
For initiating password recovery workflow, only the email field is required. The request contains the user's email address to identify the account and deliver reset instructions. The server validates the email format, checks if a user with this email exists in the todo_list_users table, generates a cryptographically secure reset token, stores it in the todo_list_password_resets table with an expiration timestamp, and sends the token to the user's email. Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent abuse, token expiration to limit vulnerability windows, and protection against email enumeration (responses don't indicate email existence).

**Password Reset Search/Filter (PATCH endpoints)**
For querying and retrieving password reset request records with filtering and pagination support. Accepts optional filter criteria including email, usage status, creation timestamps, and expiration timestamps. Supports pagination via page and limit fields, and result ordering via sort field. Used primarily for administrative monitoring, security auditing, and user account status checking. All filter and pagination fields are optional, allowing flexible query construction.

**Field Usage by Operation Type**
- Password Reset Initiation: Uses email (required), ignores all other fields
- Search Operations: All fields optional, enabling flexible filtering and pagination

The type's flexible structure with all fields optional (except email for initiation) allows it to serve both use cases efficiently while maintaining type safety and clear documentation of each field's purpose and constraints.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating that password reset instructions have been sent.

This message is intentionally generic to prevent email enumeration attacks. The response does not indicate whether the email address exists in the system or not, maintaining security by not disclosing user account information to potential attackers.

Typical message content confirms that if the email exists in the system, reset instructions have been sent to it.

ITodoListPasswordReset.IRequestResult.description:
Response body for password reset request operation.

This type represents the result returned after a user initiates the password reset process by submitting their email address. The response is designed to be secure and prevent information disclosure attacks.

Security design principles applied in this response type include protection against email enumeration attacks (the response does not reveal whether the email exists in the database), consistent response structure (same format returned regardless of email existence), and generic messaging (does not provide specific details about the reset process that could aid attackers).

The actual password reset token generation and email sending occur server-side, with the token stored in the todo_list_password_resets table. This response simply confirms that the request has been processed, without exposing sensitive implementation details.

Used as the response body for the POST /auth/user/password/reset/request endpoint.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the password reset record.

Auto-generated UUID serving as the primary key for this password reset token in the todo_list_password_resets table.
Used to track and validate password reset requests throughout their lifecycle.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the user account requesting password reset.

This field establishes the relationship between the password reset token and the specific user account in the todo_list_users table. It directly corresponds to the id field in todo_list_users, creating a one-to-many relationship where one user can have multiple password reset requests over time.

This foreign key is essential for querying password reset history, validating token ownership, and maintaining referential integrity in the database. When a password reset token is validated, this field is used to locate the correct user record to update the password.

In administrative interfaces, this field allows direct lookup of the user account without requiring email-based queries. It's particularly useful in debugging scenarios and security audits where tracing reset requests back to specific user IDs is necessary.

email.description:
Email address of the user account associated with this password reset request.

This is a computed field obtained by joining with the todo_list_users table through the todo_list_user_id foreign key relationship. While not directly stored in the todo_list_password_resets table, it provides essential context for identifying which user account requested the password reset.

Displaying the email address instead of the internal user ID improves usability in administrative interfaces and security monitoring dashboards, allowing staff to quickly identify reset requests without needing to cross-reference user IDs.

token.description:
Unique password reset token sent to the user's email.

This cryptographically secure token serves as the authentication mechanism for password reset requests. Generated during the password reset request phase, it is stored in the todo_list_password_resets table and sent to the user via email as part of a secure reset link.

The token must be kept confidential and is validated against multiple security criteria: authenticity (must exist in database), expiration (must be within validity period), and usage status (must not have been previously used). Tokens are single-use and time-limited to minimize security exposure.

In administrative interfaces and security monitoring tools, having access to the token value enables troubleshooting of reset failures, investigation of suspicious reset patterns, and verification of token delivery. While this field should never be exposed to end users in summary views, it is essential for administrative operations and security auditing.

The token is indexed in the database for efficient lookup during validation operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Used to calculate token expiration and track reset request timing.
Helps identify suspicious patterns of multiple reset requests.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token expires.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
After this time, the reset token becomes invalid and a new one must be requested.
Typically set to 1-2 hours from creation time for security reasons.

used.description:
Token usage status.

Indicates whether the password reset token has been used to successfully reset a password.
False by default when token is created, set to true upon successful password reset.
Prevents token reuse and ensures one-time use security model.

ITodoListPasswordReset.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a password reset record.

Lightweight view of password reset tokens used in administrative monitoring and status checks.
Contains essential information about pending or completed password reset requests including the full token data for administrative troubleshooting and security auditing.

Password reset tokens are created when users request account recovery through the forgot password flow.
Each token has a short lifetime for security and can only be used once.
Tracking reset status enables proper security monitoring and prevents abuse.

Used in administrative dashboards, security monitoring, and user account status displays.
Includes the reset token for administrative purposes - in end-user facing contexts, the token should be filtered out for security reasons.

Note: The email field is a computed property obtained through the relationship with todo_list_users table, not directly stored in todo_list_password_resets. The todo_list_user_id provides the foreign key reference that establishes this relationship.

token.description:
Password reset token received via email.

This token was generated during the password reset request phase and stored in the todo_list_password_resets table. The user receives this token via email as part of a secure reset link. The token serves as proof that the user has access to the email account associated with their user account.

The server validates this token against records in the todo_list_password_resets table, checking token authenticity (must exist in database), expiration status (must not have exceeded validity period), and usage status (must not have been previously used).

Tokens are single-use and time-limited for security. After successful password reset, the token is marked as used to prevent replay attacks.

newPassword.description:
New password to set for the user account.

This is the plain-text password provided by the user, which will be securely hashed by the server before being stored in the password field of the todo_list_users table. The server enforces password strength requirements to ensure account security.

Password strength validation typically includes minimum length requirements, complexity requirements (mix of characters), and checks against common password lists. After successful validation and hashing, this new password replaces the old password in the database.

For security, all existing sessions in the todo_list_user_sessions table are invalidated after password change to ensure the user must re-authenticate with the new password.

ITodoListPasswordReset.IConfirm.description:
Request body for confirming password reset and setting new password.

This type represents the data required to complete the password recovery workflow after a user has received a reset token via email. It contains both the reset token (proving email ownership) and the new password to be set.

This is the second phase of the two-phase password reset process. The server validates the reset token from the todo_list_password_resets table, verifies it has not expired or been used, updates the password in the todo_list_users table with the securely hashed new password, marks the token as used, and invalidates all existing user sessions.

Security measures include token validation (authenticity, expiration, single-use), password strength enforcement (complexity and length requirements), secure password hashing (industry-standard algorithms), session invalidation (forced re-authentication), and one-time token usage (prevention of replay attacks).

Used as the request body for the POST /auth/user/password/reset/confirm endpoint.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password reset operation completed successfully.

When true, the password has been successfully updated in the todo_list_users table and the reset token in todo_list_password_resets has been marked as used. When false, the operation failed due to invalid token, expired token, or other validation errors.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the result of the password reset operation.

Provides detailed feedback to the user about the outcome, such as 'Password successfully reset' for successful operations, or specific error messages like 'Reset token has expired' or 'Invalid reset token' for failed operations. This message can be displayed directly to the user in the client application.

ITodoListPasswordReset.IConfirmResult.description:
Response type for password reset confirmation endpoint.

Returned after validating the password reset token from todo_list_password_resets table and updating the user's password in todo_list_users table. This type represents the outcome of the password reset operation, indicating whether the new password was successfully set and providing user-friendly feedback.

This is the final response in the two-phase password recovery workflow, where users first request a reset token via email, then use this endpoint to complete the password change. The response confirms whether the token was valid and the password update succeeded.

current_password.description:
The user's current password for verification purposes.

This field is required to prove that the authenticated user knows their existing password before allowing a password change. The backend will validate this against the hashed password stored in the todo_list_users table. This verification step prevents unauthorized password changes even if someone gains access to an authenticated session.

The value should be provided in plain text as entered by the user. The backend is responsible for hashing and comparing it with the stored password hash.

new_password.description:
The new password to set for the user account.

This field contains the desired new password that will replace the current password in the todo_list_users table. The password should meet security requirements such as minimum length, character diversity, and other password strength criteria enforced by the backend.

The value should be provided in plain text as entered by the user. The backend is responsible for hashing the password using industry-standard algorithms before storing it in the database. After successful password change, the user's authentication sessions may be invalidated, requiring re-authentication with the new password.

ITodoListUser.IChangePassword.description:
Request body for authenticated password change operation.

Used when an authenticated user wants to change their password while logged in. Unlike password reset (which uses email-based token verification), this operation requires the user to provide their current password as proof of identity, along with the new password they wish to set.

This type is used with the user authentication actor, ensuring only the account owner can change their password. The current_password field provides an additional security layer beyond session authentication, preventing unauthorized password changes from compromised sessions.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password change operation completed successfully.

This boolean flag confirms that the user's password has been successfully updated in the todo_list_users table. A true value means the current password was verified, the new password met all security requirements, and the password hash was successfully updated in the database.

Clients should use this flag to determine the appropriate user feedback message and next steps in the password change workflow.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message describing the password change result.

Provides a clear, user-friendly message confirming the password change operation. This message is suitable for direct display to end users in the application interface.

Typical success messages include confirmation that the password was changed and may include additional information about security-related actions taken (such as session invalidation on other devices).

ITodoListUser.IChangePasswordResult.description:
Response confirming successful password change for authenticated user.

This response type is returned after a user successfully changes their password through the authenticated password change endpoint. It provides confirmation that the password update operation completed successfully and the new password is now active.

The response confirms that the user's current password was verified, the new password met all security requirements, and the password hash was successfully updated in the todo_list_users table. Optionally, the operation may have invalidated other active sessions, which would be indicated in the message.

email.description:
Administrator email address used for authentication and system notifications.

This email serves as the unique identifier for the admin account and is used for login authentication. It must be a valid email address format and unique across all administrator accounts in the todo_list_admins table.

The email is used for critical system communications, password reset workflows, and as the primary credential for admin authentication. It cannot be changed after account creation without special procedures.

password.description:
Plain text password for the administrator account that will be securely hashed before storage.

This is the administrator's chosen password provided during registration. The password must meet minimum security requirements including a minimum length of 8 characters. The system should enforce additional password complexity rules such as requiring a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

The plain text password is only transmitted during registration and is immediately hashed using industry-standard cryptographic algorithms (such as bcrypt or Argon2) before being stored in the todo_list_admins table's password field. The plain text password is never stored or logged.

ip.description:
IP address of the client creating the admin account for session tracking and audit purposes.

This optional field captures the IP address from which the admin registration request originates. It is used for security auditing and session management in the todo_list_admin_sessions table.

The server can automatically extract this from the HTTP request headers, but clients may provide it explicitly for scenarios like server-side rendering or proxy configurations. The IP address helps track admin account creation for security monitoring and can be used to detect suspicious registration patterns.

href.description:
Current page URL where the admin registration is taking place.

This required field captures the full URL of the page or application context where the admin account creation is initiated. It is stored as part of the session information in the todo_list_admin_sessions table for audit trail and security monitoring purposes.

The href helps track where admin registrations occur within the application, which is valuable for security analysis and understanding user behavior. It must be a valid URI format.

referrer.description:
URL of the previous page that led to the admin registration page.

This required field captures the referrer URL, indicating how the admin arrived at the registration page. It is stored as part of the session metadata in the todo_list_admin_sessions table.

The referrer information helps understand the registration flow and can be useful for security monitoring to detect unusual registration patterns. For direct navigation to the registration page, this may be an empty string. It must be a valid URI format when provided.

ITodoListAdmin.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new system administrator account with authentication credentials and session context.

This DTO contains all necessary information to register a new administrator in the system. It includes authentication credentials (email and password) that will be used for future admin logins, along with session context information (IP, href, referrer) that establishes the initial admin session.

The password provided in this DTO is in plain text and will be securely hashed by the backend before being stored in the todo_list_admins table. The session context fields enable proper tracking of the admin registration event and creation of the initial session record in the todo_list_admin_sessions table.

This is a self-registration DTO where the admin themselves are creating their account, hence the inclusion of session context fields (ip, href, referrer) which are required for self-authentication operations.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Successful authentication response containing JWT tokens for administrator access.

This schema represents the response returned after successful admin authentication operations including login and token refresh. It contains both an access token for authorizing API requests and a refresh token for obtaining new access tokens when the current one expires.

The access token is a short-lived JWT that should be included in the Authorization header of subsequent API requests. The refresh token is a long-lived credential used exclusively for obtaining new access tokens through the refresh endpoint.

Clients should store the access token for immediate use in API calls and securely store the refresh token for long-term session maintenance. When the access token expires, clients should use the refresh token to obtain a new access token without requiring the administrator to re-authenticate with email and password.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated administrator account.

This ID corresponds to the primary key in the todo_list_admins table and uniquely identifies the admin user throughout the system. Clients can use this ID to make subsequent API calls that require the admin's identity, such as fetching admin profile information or performing admin-specific operations.

The ID is included in the response to allow clients to immediately identify which admin account has been authenticated without requiring an additional API call.

email.description:
Administrator's email address for account communications and recovery.

Must be a valid email format and unique across all administrator accounts. Used for password reset workflows, security notifications, and administrative communications.

This email serves as the primary identifier for the admin account and is used for login authentication. It corresponds to the email column in the todo_list_admins table.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was created.

Auto-generated by the system upon account creation. Used for audit trails, account lifecycle tracking, and compliance reporting.

This field is immutable after creation and corresponds to the created_at column in the todo_list_admins table. Returned in ISO 8601 date-time format.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator account information was last modified.

Automatically updated by the system whenever any admin account field is changed, such as password updates or email modifications. Used for tracking account changes, audit logging, and data synchronization.

This field corresponds to the updated_at column in the todo_list_admins table and is automatically managed by the database. Returned in ISO 8601 date-time format.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was soft-deleted.

Null for active accounts, set to deletion time for removed accounts. Enables soft deletion pattern to preserve audit trails and historical data while excluding the account from normal operations.

Supports potential account restoration if needed. Corresponds to the deleted_at column in the todo_list_admins table.

email.description:
Administrator's email address for authentication.

Must be a valid email format and correspond to an existing admin account in the todo_list_admins table. This serves as the unique username for administrator login.

password.description:
Administrator's password in plain text for verification.

The password is transmitted securely (over HTTPS) and verified against the hashed password stored in the database. The server performs cryptographic comparison to validate credentials without exposing the stored hash.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for Server-Side Rendering scenarios, though the server can typically extract this from the request headers. Used for audit logging, suspicious activity detection, and session management in the todo_list_admin_sessions table.

href.description:
Current page URL where the login is being performed.

Mandatory connection context field that records the web page from which the administrator is logging in. This helps track user authentication flows, detect potential phishing attempts, and maintain proper session context in the todo_list_admin_sessions table.

referrer.description:
Previous page URL that directed to the login page.

Mandatory connection context field that records where the administrator came from before reaching the login page. Can be an empty string for direct access. Used for analytics, security monitoring, and understanding authentication entry points.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Administrator login credentials with session context information.

Used for authenticating existing administrator accounts. Contains the email and password for credential verification, plus connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) for session tracking and security purposes.

The session context fields (href and referrer) are mandatory as they establish proper audit trails and enable security monitoring. The IP address is optional since the server can extract it from request headers, though clients may provide it explicitly in Server-Side Rendering scenarios.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for obtaining new JWT access tokens.

This schema represents the request body for the admin token refresh operation. It contains the refresh token that was previously issued during login or the last token refresh. The refresh token is a long-lived credential that allows administrators to obtain new short-lived access tokens without re-entering their credentials.

The refresh token should be stored securely by the client (typically in httpOnly cookies or secure storage) and transmitted to this endpoint when the access token expires or is about to expire. The backend validates the refresh token against the todo_list_admin_sessions table to ensure it exists, hasn't expired, and corresponds to a valid admin account.

Security considerations: The refresh token must be kept confidential and transmitted only over secure connections. Clients should implement proper token storage and rotation strategies to minimize the risk of token theft or replay attacks.

refreshToken.description:
The refresh token previously issued during administrator login or token refresh.

This token is validated against the todo_list_admin_sessions table to verify it exists, hasn't expired, and corresponds to an active admin session. If valid, the system issues a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token) allowing continued authenticated access without requiring password re-entry.

The refresh token format is typically a secure random string or JWT that contains session identification information. It has a longer lifespan than access tokens (often days or weeks compared to minutes or hours) but can be revoked if security concerns arise.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account.

Generated automatically upon account creation using UUID v4 format. This identifier is immutable and serves as the primary key for the user entity across all system operations and relationships.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication and communication.
