Used for sending account notifications, verification emails, and system communications.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status indicating whether the user has confirmed their email address.

Users must verify their email address before accessing full application features. This field is set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the user successfully completes the email verification workflow by clicking the verification link sent to their email.

Email verification is a critical security measure that confirms the user has access to the email address they provided during registration. Unverified accounts may have limited functionality or be subject to additional security restrictions.

Used to enforce email verification requirements and determine access levels for user accounts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the user account was created.

Automatically set by the system upon account registration. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. This field is immutable and used for audit trails and account age calculations.

Provides historical context for user lifecycle management and analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of when the user account information was last modified.

Automatically updated by the system whenever any user account field is changed, including email updates, password changes, or verification status modifications. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This field enables change tracking and audit trail functionality, allowing administrators and users to understand when account modifications occurred. Useful for security monitoring and compliance reporting.

Updated automatically by the database on any UPDATE operation to the user record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the user account was marked as deleted.

When set, indicates the user account has been deleted but preserved for audit purposes and data integrity. Null for active accounts. The soft deletion pattern allows the system to maintain referential integrity and historical records while logically removing the account from normal operations.

Soft-deleted accounts are excluded from login operations and user listings but remain in the database for compliance, audit trails, and potential account recovery scenarios. This approach is preferable to hard deletion for regulatory compliance and data protection requirements.

Deleted accounts may be subject to permanent removal after a retention period as defined by data governance policies.

ITodoListUser.description:
Complete user account entity representing an authenticated user in the Todo application.

This entity represents registered users who can create and manage todo items. Users authenticate using email and password credentials, with the system maintaining secure password hashing. Each user account has a unique identifier and email address.

The user entity serves as the primary actor for todo ownership and management. All todo items are associated with their creator through the user relationship. User accounts track creation and modification timestamps for audit and lifecycle management purposes, along with email verification status to ensure account security.

Security considerations include password protection (password_hash field excluded from responses), email uniqueness enforcement, and email verification requirements. The entity integrates with the session management system for authentication state tracking and supports soft deletion for compliance and audit purposes.

Used in response bodies for user retrieval operations, account updates, and authentication flows. Related entities include todo_list_user_sessions for session tracking and todo_list_todos for task ownership.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all users in the system. Updates to email may trigger re-verification workflows if the system requires email confirmation. The email serves as the primary identifier for password recovery and account notifications.

Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards to ensure deliverability.

password.description:
User's new password for authentication security.

Provided as plain text in the request and securely hashed by the backend before storage in the password_hash column. Password changes trigger security notifications and may invalidate existing sessions depending on security policy.

Must meet minimum security requirements including length constraints. The backend is responsible for hashing and storing this value securely using bcrypt with minimum cost factor of 10.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying user account information.

This DTO contains the optional fields that can be modified on an existing user account. All fields are optional to support partial updates where only specific attributes need to be changed. Unchanged fields retain their existing values in the database.

Password updates are handled securely with the backend performing hashing before storage. Email updates may trigger verification workflows to confirm ownership of the new email address and are validated for uniqueness and format compliance.

Used in PUT operations for both user self-service account updates and administrative user management functions.

page.description:
Page number for pagination of session results.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when session listings exceed the page size limit. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in conjunction with limit to implement offset-based pagination.

Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return per page.

Controls the page size for paginated session listings. Enforces a maximum value to prevent excessive data transfer and maintain system performance. Typical values range from 10 to 50 for optimal user experience.

Defaults to a sensible value (typically 20) if not specified.

sort_by.description:
Field to use for sorting the session results.

Currently supports sorting by session creation time (created_at) based on available fields in the todo_list_user_sessions table. Sessions can be ordered chronologically to identify newest or oldest sessions first.

Defaults to created_at when not specified.

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction for session results.

Defaults to desc for most use cases.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by IP address.

Optional filter for targeted session searches.

created_after.description:

Allows restricting results to sessions created after a specific date and time. Useful for analyzing recent session activity or investigating security events within a time window. Expected in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

Optional temporal filter for session queries.

created_before.description:
Filter to include only sessions created before this timestamp.

Allows restricting results to sessions created before a specific date and time. Combined with created_after enables time-range filtering for historical session analysis. Expected in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

Optional temporal filter for session queries.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering user authentication sessions.

This DTO defines the query parameters for retrieving a filtered and paginated list of active user sessions. Supports comprehensive filtering by temporal criteria (creation date ranges) and network information (IP address). Pagination and sorting controls enable efficient browsing of potentially large session collections.

The search functionality is designed for security monitoring use cases where users or administrators need to identify active sessions across different devices and locations. All filter parameters are optional, with sensible defaults applied when not specified. Session data is sourced from the todo_list_user_sessions table which tracks connection details including IP address, connection URL, referrer, and timestamps.

Used in PATCH operations for session listing endpoints that return paginated results. The parameters enable both user self-service session management and administrative security monitoring workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user session.

This UUID uniquely identifies each authentication session created when a user logs into the Todo list application. The session ID is used for tracking active sessions and validating authenticated requests.

Corresponds to the primary key in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the authenticated user who owns this session.

IP address from which the session connection was established.

href.description:

Records the specific application URL where the user initiated their authentication. Useful for understanding user login patterns and detecting potential security issues.

Stored in URI format for standardized URL representation.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the session creation.

Captures the previous page URL before the user accessed the login screen. Helps track user navigation flows and identify traffic sources.

Stored in URI format following standard HTTP referrer header conventions.

created_at.description:
Session creation timestamp when the user successfully authenticated.

Records the exact date and time when the user successfully authenticated and the session was established. Used for session age calculations, audit logging, and security monitoring.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format for universal compatibility.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp when the session ended or was terminated.

For active sessions, this field is null, indicating the session is still valid and has not been terminated. For expired or terminated sessions, contains the ISO 8601 timestamp when the session became invalid.

Used to distinguish between active sessions (null value) and terminated sessions (datetime value) for session management and security workflows.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:

Provides essential session information for authenticated users in the Todo list application. This lightweight DTO is used in authentication responses, session listings, and contexts where full session details are not required.

Contains core session metadata including session identifier, associated user reference, connection context (IP, href, referrer), creation timestamp, and expiration status. The summary variant excludes the authentication token and nested user object while providing sufficient information for session tracking and user context identification.

Used primarily in authentication flows, session validation endpoints, and as nested references within other DTOs that need to show active session context.

id.description:

This UUID is automatically generated when a user successfully authenticates and establishes a new session. It serves as the primary key for session tracking and validation throughout the session lifecycle.

Corresponds to the primary key in the todo_list_user_sessions Prisma table.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the authenticated user who owns this session.

This field establishes the relationship between the session and the user account in the todo_list_users table. It ensures that each session is properly associated with exactly one user account and enables session queries by user.

Matches the Prisma schema foreign key column name for data layer consistency.

ip.description:
IP address from which the session connection was established.

Captures the client IP address at the time of session creation for security audit trails and monitoring. Essential for detecting suspicious login patterns, tracking geographic access patterns, and investigating security incidents.

Stores both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in string format as recorded in the Prisma schema.

href.description:
Connection URL where the session was initiated.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the session creation.

Captures the HTTP referrer header value indicating which page or source directed the user to the authentication flow. Valuable for understanding user navigation patterns and traffic source attribution.

Follows URI format standards as defined in the Prisma schema.

token.description:
Authentication token used for API request authorization.

This token is a secure, cryptographically-generated string (typically a JWT) that clients include in request headers to prove their authenticated identity. The token contains encoded session information and is validated on each API request to authorized endpoints.

Note: This is a computed/virtual field not directly stored in the Prisma schema but derived from session data for API authentication purposes.

created_at.description:
Session creation timestamp when the user successfully authenticated.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime records the exact moment the user successfully authenticated and the session was established. It is used for session age calculations, audit logging, and security monitoring.

Directly corresponds to the created_at column in the Prisma schema.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp when the session ended or was terminated.

For active sessions, this field is null, indicating ongoing validity. For terminated or expired sessions, contains the ISO 8601 timestamp marking when the session became invalid and the user lost authenticated access.

Session expiration is a critical security mechanism to limit exposure windows for token compromise. Null values indicate active sessions, while datetime values indicate session termination through logout, timeout, or administrative action.

user.description:
Summary information about the user who owns this authentication session.

This nested object provides essential user details associated with the session, enabling clients to display user context without requiring additional API calls. It includes basic user identification and profile information.

Represents the relationship to the todo_list_users table through the todo_list_user_id foreign key.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session entity for registered users in the Todo list application.

Represents an active authentication session established when a user successfully logs in. Each session contains connection context (IP address, referrer, href), authentication credentials (token), and temporal information (creation and expiration timestamps) defining the session's validity period.

Sessions are created during login operations and can be explicitly terminated through logout or deleted by administrators for security purposes. The session entity maintains the relationship between authentication tokens and user accounts, enabling secure, stateless API authentication.

When a session expires or is deleted, the associated token becomes invalid, requiring the user to re-authenticate. Active sessions have a null expired_at field, while terminated sessions contain the termination timestamp.

This entity corresponds to the todo_list_user_sessions table in the Prisma schema and is central to the application's authentication and authorization infrastructure. Sessions can be retrieved individually for verification, listed for session management, and deleted for logout or security enforcement workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the registered user.

This UUID is automatically generated when a user account is created and serves as the primary key for identifying authenticated users throughout the application.

email.description:
User's email address.

Used for authentication, communication, and account identification.
Must be unique across all users in the system and validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status for the user account.

Indicates whether the user has verified their email address through the verification process. Users must verify their email before accessing full application features.

This boolean flag is used to enforce email verification requirements and control access to protected functionality. Unverified users may have restricted capabilities until they complete the email verification workflow.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format, this indicates when the user first registered with the Todo list application.
Useful for account age tracking, analytics, and sorting users by registration date.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account information was last modified.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format, this tracks the most recent update to any user account field including profile information, email, or authentication settings.
Useful for tracking account activity, detecting stale accounts, and audit logging purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the user account.

When set, indicates the user account has been deleted but preserved for audit purposes and data integrity. Deleted accounts are excluded from normal operations but maintained for historical records.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a registered user account.

Users represent authenticated individuals who have registered accounts and can create and manage their personal todo items.

Used in list views, todo item ownership displays, user selection interfaces, and administrative dashboards where full user details are unnecessary.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator account.

email.description:
Administrator's email address for communication and account recovery.

created_at.description:

Useful for tracking account changes, detecting inactive administrators, and maintaining audit trails for security compliance.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for administrator accounts.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing administrator account's information.

This DTO defines the modifiable fields for administrator account updates. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates where only specified fields are modified while others remain unchanged. The operation supports updating administrator profile information including email and password credentials.

Email updates must follow valid email format and maintain uniqueness across all administrator accounts. Password updates should provide the new plain-text password which will be securely hashed by the backend before storage.

Field validation ensures emails are properly formatted and passwords meet strength requirements. The system validates uniqueness constraints before applying changes to prevent conflicts.

Used in administrator profile update operations, credential rotation workflows, and administrative account management interfaces.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity representing system administrators in the Todo list application.

This entity represents authenticated administrator accounts with elevated privileges for managing the Todo list application. Administrators have access to system-wide management functions including user management, system configuration, and administrative operations.

The admin entity stores core identity information including unique identifier, email address for communications and account recovery, and securely hashed password for authentication. The entity tracks account lifecycle through creation, modification, and deletion timestamps, supporting soft deletion to preserve audit trails.

Administrators authenticate through dedicated admin login endpoints and maintain separate session management via the todo_list_admin_sessions table. The password_hash field uses secure cryptographic hashing algorithms and is never exposed in API responses.

Used in administrator management interfaces, authentication flows, audit logging, and system administration dashboards.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrator account.

Auto-generated UUID serving as the primary key for the admin record. Used for referencing the admin in relationships, API operations, and security contexts.

email.description:

updated_at.description:

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was soft-deleted.

Null for active accounts, set to deletion time for removed accounts. Enables soft deletion pattern to preserve audit trails and historical data while excluding the account from normal operations. Supports potential account restoration if needed.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Administrator authentication session entity representing an active login session for a system administrator.

This entity captures comprehensive session information including session timestamps (creation and expiration), client connection details (IP address, connection URL, and referrer), and the relationship to the administrator account. Sessions are created during the administrator login process and remain active until they expire naturally, are explicitly terminated through logout, or are revoked for security reasons. The session entity is critical for authentication state management, security auditing, and access control enforcement throughout the application.

This type is used in session retrieval operations, session management workflows, and authentication state validation. It provides complete session details including all authentication metadata and client information necessary for security monitoring and audit trail purposes.

href.description:

Useful for tracking admin navigation flows, identifying traffic sources to administrative interfaces, and detecting unusual access patterns. Empty string indicates direct navigation to the login page without a referrer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created.

Records the exact date and time when the administrator authenticated and this session was established. This timestamp is used for session age calculations, audit logging, and security monitoring to identify long-running sessions.

Automatically set by the system during session creation and remains immutable throughout the session lifecycle.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or will expire.

For active sessions, indicates the future date and time when this session will automatically become invalid and require re-authentication. For terminated sessions, records when the session was ended.

Session expiration is a security measure to limit the lifetime of authentication and reduce the window of opportunity for session compromise. Null value indicates a currently active session that has not yet expired.

admin.description:

Provides essential details about the authenticated administrator including their email and account information. This associated data eliminates the need for separate API calls to retrieve administrator context when working with session information.

Used for displaying administrator details alongside session data in administrative dashboards and audit interfaces.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the admin session.

todo_list_admin_id.description:

ITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying administrator session records.

This request DTO enables comprehensive filtering and retrieval of administrator sessions with support for pagination, sorting, and multiple search criteria. It allows filtering sessions by creation date ranges, expiration timestamps, and IP addresses. These capabilities support security monitoring workflows, session management interfaces, and administrative oversight of authentication activity.

Typical use cases include: retrieving all active sessions for security auditing, finding sessions from specific IP addresses to investigate suspicious activity, listing sessions by creation date for compliance reporting, and paginating through session history for administrative review.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the total number of matching sessions exceeds the page size limit. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of sessions to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 100 records per page. Smaller limits improve response times for large result sets while larger limits reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all data.

sort.description:
Array of sort specifications in format 'field' or '-field' for descending order.

Defines the sorting order for the result set. Each element specifies a field name, optionally prefixed with '-' for descending sort. Examples: ['created_at'] for ascending by creation date, ['-created_at'] for newest first, ['ip', '-created_at'] for multi-field sorting.

search.description:
General search term for text-based filtering.

Enables fuzzy matching across searchable text fields such as IP addresses, href URLs, and referrer URLs. Useful for quickly finding sessions matching partial connection information.

created_at_after.description:
Filter sessions created after this timestamp (inclusive).

Returns only sessions where the creation timestamp is greater than or equal to the specified date-time. Useful for retrieving recent sessions or filtering by specific time periods.

created_at_before.description:
Filter sessions created before this timestamp (inclusive).

Returns only sessions where the creation timestamp is less than or equal to the specified date-time. Combines with created_at_after to define date ranges for session queries.

expired_at_after.description:
Filter sessions expiring after this timestamp (inclusive).

Returns sessions that will remain valid beyond the specified date-time. Useful for identifying long-lived sessions or filtering out sessions that are about to expire.

expired_at_before.description:
Filter sessions expiring before this timestamp (inclusive).

Returns sessions that will expire by the specified date-time. Useful for identifying sessions nearing expiration or filtering by session duration.

ip.description:
Filter by exact IP address match.

Returns only sessions created from the specified IP address. Critical for security investigations to identify all sessions originating from a particular network location.

id.description:

todo_list_user_id.description:
Identifier of the user account associated with this email verification.

This foreign key links the verification record to the specific user account in the todo_list_users table, establishing ownership of the verification attempt. References the id field in todo_list_users.

token.description:
Unique verification token sent to the user's email address.

This cryptographically secure token is included in the verification email link. When users click the verification link, this token is validated to confirm email ownership. The token is single-use and has an expiration time for security purposes.

verified.description:
Whether this verification token has been successfully used.

Indicates the current verification status: true if the user has completed email verification by using this token, false if the verification is still pending. Once verified, the token cannot be reused to prevent security issues.

created_at.description:

Records when this verification record was created in the system, providing an audit trail for email verification attempts and helping track the verification workflow timeline.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this verification token expires.

Tokens are valid for 24 hours after creation. After this date and time, the verification token becomes invalid and cannot be used to verify the email address. Users must request a new verification email if the token has expired.

ITodoListEmailVerification.description:
Email verification token entity for user account activation.

Stores unique verification tokens sent to users during registration to confirm email ownership. Each token is associated with a user account and has a limited validity period for security purposes.

When a user registers, the system generates a verification token and sends it via email. Users must click the verification link containing the token to activate their account and gain full access to the application.

Tokens expire after 24 hours to prevent abuse. Expired tokens require users to request a new verification email. Once a token is successfully used for verification, it becomes invalid to prevent reuse.

This entity corresponds to the todo_list_email_verifications table in the Prisma schema and supports the email verification workflow for user account activation and security.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the email verification record.

Auto-generated UUID serving as the primary key for this verification token.
Used to track and validate email verification requests throughout their lifecycle.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Reference to the user account requiring email verification.

Foreign key linking this verification record to the associated user in the todo_list_users table.
This establishes ownership of the verification token and determines which account will be activated upon successful verification.

The relationship is mandatory - every email verification must be associated with a specific user account.
Used to retrieve user details and update account status during the verification workflow.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the verification token was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Used to calculate token expiration and track verification request timing.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when the verification token expires.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
After this time, the verification token becomes invalid and a new one must be requested.
Typically set to 24-48 hours from creation time.

verified.description:
Verification completion status.

Indicates whether the email address has been successfully verified.
False by default when token is created, set to true upon successful verification.
Used to prevent token reuse and track verification state.

ITodoListEmailVerification.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an email verification record.

Lightweight view of email verification tokens used in list displays and embedded references.
Contains essential information about pending or completed email verifications without exposing sensitive token data.

Email verifications are created when users register new accounts and require email confirmation.
Each verification has a limited lifetime and can only be used once.
Tracking verification status enables proper account activation workflows and security measures.

Used in verification status checks, account activation flows, and administrative monitoring of pending verifications.
Excludes the actual verification token for security reasons - token is only exposed during creation.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve, starting from 1. Used in conjunction with limit to implement offset-based pagination through large result sets.

limit.description:
Number of records per page.

Controls how many email verification records are returned in a single page. Maximum value is capped at 100 to prevent performance issues with large result sets.

search.description:
Search term for filtering verification records.

Performs text search across related user email addresses to find specific verification records. Useful for locating verification attempts for particular email addresses or email domains.

verified.description:
Filter by verification status.

When true, returns only completed verifications (verified field is true). When false, returns only pending verifications (verified field is false). When null or omitted, returns all verification records regardless of status.

expired.description:
Filter by expiration status.

When true, returns only expired verification tokens (expires_at is in the past). When false, returns only non-expired tokens (expires_at is in the future). When null or omitted, returns all verification records regardless of expiration status.

oneOf.description:
Sort by creation timestamp.

Orders verification records by the time they were created (created_at field).
Useful for finding recent verification attempts or reviewing verification history chronologically.

Sort by expiration timestamp.

Orders verification records by their expiration time (expires_at field).
Useful for identifying tokens that are about to expire or have recently expired.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines which timestamp field is used for ordering the verification records. Available options are creation date (created_at) or expiration date (expires_at).

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort order.

Sorts results from oldest to newest based on the sort_by field.
Useful for reviewing historical verification records in chronological order.

Descending sort order.

Sorts results from newest to oldest based on the sort_by field.
Descending order shows most recent records first, which is typically the default preference.

order.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Descending order shows most recent records first.

ITodoListEmailVerification.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering email verification records.

Provides comprehensive search, filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities for retrieving email verification records. All parameters are optional, with sensible defaults applied when not specified.

Supports filtering by verification status (verified/pending) and expiration status (expired/active). Text search capability allows finding verification records by searching related user email addresses. Pagination controls allow efficient navigation through large result sets with configurable page sizes.

Sorting options enable ordering by creation date or expiration date in either ascending or descending order. This flexibility supports various use cases including finding recent verification attempts, identifying expired tokens, or tracking verification completion history.

ITodoListPasswordReset.description:
Password reset request entity for user account recovery in the Todo list application.

Represents a time-limited password reset token generated when a user requests to reset their password. Each reset request is uniquely identified and contains security information including the reset token, expiration timestamp, and usage status.

Password reset requests are created when users initiate the password recovery workflow, typically by clicking a "Forgot Password" link. The reset token is sent to the user's verified email address and must be used before the expiration time. Once used or expired, the reset request becomes invalid.

This entity implements security best practices including token expiration, single-use tokens, and secure random token generation. Reset requests are permanently associated with the user who initiated them and track whether the reset has been completed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the password reset request.

Generated automatically by the system when a password reset is initiated. This UUID serves as the primary key for the reset request record.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Identifier of the user account requesting password reset.

Foreign key reference to the todo_list_users table. Links this reset request to the specific user account that initiated the password recovery process.

token.description:
Secure random token used to verify password reset authorization.

Cryptographically secure random string that serves as the authorization mechanism for password reset. This token is sent to the user's email and must be provided to complete the password reset process. The token should be treated as sensitive information and transmitted securely.

used.description:
Indicates whether this password reset token has been successfully used.

Boolean flag that tracks the usage status of the reset token. When false, the token is available for use (subject to expiration). When true, the token has been consumed to reset the password and cannot be reused.

This prevents token reuse attacks where an attacker might attempt to use the same reset token multiple times. Once a password reset is completed, this flag is set to true permanently.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

ISO 8601 date-time automatically set when the reset request is initiated. Used to track when the user requested the password reset and to calculate expiration time.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token expires.

ISO 8601 date-time indicating when the reset token becomes invalid. Typically set to a short duration (e.g., 1 hour, 24 hours) after creation to limit the window of vulnerability. After this time, the user must request a new password reset.

ITodoListGuest.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving guest visitor records in the Todo list application.

Provides comprehensive filtering, searching, sorting, and pagination capabilities for administrative analysis of unauthenticated visitors. Supports querying by IP address patterns, visit date ranges, and various sorting options to enable detailed guest analytics.

This request structure is used exclusively by administrative operations to monitor visitor activity, analyze traffic patterns, and identify potential security concerns or conversion opportunities.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description:
Number of guest records per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Maximum value is typically 100 to prevent excessive data transfer. Defaults to a reasonable value (e.g., 20) if not specified.

search.description:
General search term for filtering guest records.

Searches across multiple fields including IP addresses and other guest metadata. Performs case-insensitive partial matching to help administrators quickly find specific guest records.

ip_address.description:
Filter by specific IP address or IP address pattern.

Allows filtering guest records by exact IP address match or pattern matching. Useful for tracking visitors from specific locations or investigating potential security issues.

visit_date_from.description:
Filter guests who visited on or after this date.

ISO 8601 date-time for the start of the visit date range filter. Used in combination with visit_date_to to analyze traffic patterns over specific time periods.

visit_date_to.description:
Filter guests who visited on or before this date.

ISO 8601 date-time for the end of the visit date range filter. Used in combination with visit_date_from to analyze traffic patterns over specific time periods.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort guest records by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering results. Available options: 'created_at' (visit timestamp) or 'ip_address' (alphabetical).

Field to sort guest records by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering results. Available options: 'created_at' (visit timestamp) or 'ip_address' (alphabetical).

sort_by.description:
Field to sort guest records by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering results. Available options: 'created_at' (visit timestamp) or 'ip_address' (alphabetical).

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Specifies ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order for the sorted results. Defaults to descending when sorting by created_at (newest first).

Sort direction for the results.

Specifies ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order for the sorted results. Defaults to descending when sorting by created_at (newest first).

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Specifies ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order for the sorted results. Defaults to descending when sorting by created_at (newest first).

id.description:
Unique identifier for the guest visitor.

This UUID is automatically generated when a guest session is created and is used to track unauthenticated users' interactions with the todo application.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the guest visitor for tracking and security purposes.

Captures the network address from which the guest is accessing the application, used for analytics and security monitoring purposes.

This field may be null if IP address information was not captured or is unavailable for privacy reasons.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string identifying the client application and device type.

Captures the HTTP User-Agent header provided by the visitor's browser or client application. This information is valuable for understanding the devices, browsers, and platforms used by visitors.

User agent data supports device-specific analytics, browser compatibility tracking, and identifying automated bot traffic. This field may be null if user agent information was not provided by the client or is unavailable.

visited_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest first visited the application.

Records the initial visit time in ISO 8601 format, marking the moment when the unauthenticated visitor first accessed any page of the application.

This timestamp is essential for analyzing visitor behavior patterns, calculating time-to-conversion metrics, and understanding peak traffic periods. It differs from created_at in that it represents the actual visit time rather than when the database record was created.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest record was created in the system.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format, this marks when the guest tracking record was inserted into the database, which typically occurs shortly after or simultaneously with the initial visit.

This system-generated timestamp is used for database auditing, record lifecycle tracking, and ensuring data consistency.

ITodoListGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an unauthenticated guest visitor.

This lightweight type is used for listing guest sessions and tracking visitor information in the Todo list application. Guests represent unauthenticated users who have not yet created an account or logged in.

Provides essential identification and tracking information for analytics and session management purposes. Used in list views, analytics dashboards, and visitor tracking contexts where full guest details are not needed.

ITodoListGuest.description:
Guest visitor entity representing unauthenticated visitors to the Todo list application.

This entity captures information about anonymous users who access the application without creating an account. Guest records are essential for analytics, security monitoring, and understanding visitor behavior patterns before account registration.

Guest tracking enables the application to monitor traffic patterns, identify potential security concerns, and analyze user acquisition funnels. Each guest session is uniquely identified and associated with connection metadata including IP address, user agent, and visit timestamps.

This entity is used in administrative operations for visitor analytics and security monitoring. It provides a foundation for understanding unauthenticated user engagement with the application.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the guest visitor record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for guest tracking and is automatically generated upon first visit. The identifier enables precise tracking of individual visitor sessions and supports correlation with other system events.

Used throughout the system to reference specific guest sessions in analytics, security logs, and conversion tracking workflows.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the guest visitor for tracking and security purposes.

Captures the network address from which the visitor accessed the application. This information is essential for security monitoring, geographic analytics, and fraud prevention.

IP addresses are handled in accordance with privacy policies and data protection regulations. They may be used for rate limiting, abuse prevention, and legitimate security purposes. This field may be null if IP address information was not captured or is unavailable.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string identifying the client application and device type.

Captures the HTTP User-Agent header sent by the visitor's browser or client application during their session. This metadata provides insights into the technologies, devices, and platforms visitors use to access the application.

User agent information supports comprehensive analytics including browser compatibility analysis, mobile vs desktop traffic patterns, and identification of automated bots or scrapers. The data helps inform technology stack decisions and user experience optimization strategies.

This field may be null if the client did not provide user agent information or if it was intentionally omitted for privacy reasons.

visited_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest first visited the application.

Records the precise moment when the unauthenticated visitor initially accessed the application, captured in ISO 8601 date-time format. This timestamp represents the actual visit event rather than database record creation time.

The visited_at field is critical for temporal analytics, including visitor flow analysis, conversion funnel timing, peak traffic identification, and session duration calculations. It provides the temporal anchor for understanding visitor behavior and engagement patterns.

This timestamp is immutable once set and serves as the definitive record of when visitor engagement began.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest visitor record was created in the system.

Indicates the exact moment when the database record for this guest was inserted, automatically set by the system. This timestamp is immutable and serves as an audit trail for record creation.

Used for database management, data lifecycle tracking, and ensuring referential integrity across the system. In most cases, this will be very close to or identical to visited_at, but they serve different purposes in the data model.

ITodoListAdmin.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering system administrator accounts.

This request type supports comprehensive querying capabilities for administrator list operations, enabling advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination. It provides flexible search criteria to locate administrators based on email address and registration dates.

The request structure supports efficient data retrieval with pagination controls and sorting options, optimized for administrative dashboard interfaces and bulk management operations.

Used in search operations to retrieve filtered lists of administrators with appropriate pagination and ordering.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the filtered administrator set. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

Defaults to 1 if not specified, returning the first page of results.

limit.description:
Number of administrator records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, allowing customization of result density. Must be between 1 and 100 to balance performance and usability.

Defaults to a reasonable value (typically 20-50) if not specified. Higher limits may impact response times for large datasets.

search.description:
General search term for filtering administrators.

Performs partial matching across administrator email addresses. The search is typically case-insensitive and supports substring matching.

Useful for quick lookup of administrators when searching by email address or email domain patterns.

email.description:
Filter administrators by email address (partial match supported).

Searches for administrators whose email contains the specified text. Supports domain-based filtering (e.g., '@company.com') or specific email pattern matching.

Enables filtering administrators by email domain, which is useful for organization-based access management.

oneOf.description:
Sort order for the administrator list results.

Specifies the field and direction for ordering results. Prefix with '-' for descending order, or use field name alone for ascending order.

Available sort options:
- 'created_at': Sort by registration date, oldest first
- '-created_at': Sort by registration date, newest first

Defaults to '-created_at' (newest administrators first) if not specified.

Defaults to '-created_at' (newest administrators first) if not specified.

sort.description:
Sort order for the administrator list results.

- '-created_at': Sort by registration date, newest first

Defaults to '-created_at' (newest administrators first) if not specified.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Determines which page of results to retrieve from the complete user list.

Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Used in conjunction with limit to control pagination. For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns users 1-20, page=2 returns users 21-40.

limit.description:
Number of users to return per page. Controls the page size for pagination results.

Must be between 1 and 100 to balance performance and usability. Smaller values reduce response payload size, larger values reduce number of requests needed. Default value of 20 is recommended for most use cases.

search.description:
Search term for partial matching across email field. Enables administrators to find user accounts by typing partial email addresses.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching on the email column. For example, searching 'john' would match 'john@example.com' and 'alice@johncompany.com'. Search is optimized with database indexes for fast query performance.

email.description:
Filter users by exact or partial email address match. Enables searching for users by their email address or email domain.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching on the email field. Can be used to find all users from a specific domain (e.g., '@company.com') or to locate a specific user's email.

email_verified.description:
Filter users by email verification status. Controls whether to retrieve only verified users, only unverified users, or all users regardless of verification status.

When true, returns only users who have verified their email addresses. When false, returns only users with unverified emails. When null or omitted, returns all users regardless of verification status.

created_after.description:
Filter users registered after this date and time. Enables querying users who joined the platform after a specific timestamp.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z'). Used in conjunction with created_before to define date ranges for user registration analysis.

created_before.description:
Filter users registered before this date and time. Enables querying users who joined the platform before a specific timestamp.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). Used in conjunction with created_after to define date ranges for user registration analysis.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the user list by. Determines the ordering criteria for the returned user results.

Supported values: 'created_at' (registration date), 'email' (alphabetical by email). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Field to sort the user list by. Determines the ordering criteria for the returned user results.

Supported values: 'created_at' (registration date), 'email' (alphabetical by email). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

order_by.description:
Field to sort the user list by. Determines the ordering criteria for the returned user results.

Supported values: 'created_at' (registration date), 'email' (alphabetical by email). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the order_by field. Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order.

'asc' for ascending order (oldest first for dates, A-Z for text). 'desc' for descending order (newest first for dates, Z-A for text). Defaults to 'desc' for created_at, 'asc' for text fields.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering the user list with pagination support. Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for administrative user management.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters with configurable page sizes. Enables flexible searching through general search term or specific email field filter. Allows filtering by email verification status and registration date ranges. Provides sorting options by created_at and email fields in ascending or descending order.

All filter parameters are optional and can be combined for complex queries. The search and email filter work together to narrow results. Date range filters (created_after, created_before) can be used independently or together to define precise time windows.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Determines which page of todo results to retrieve from the user's complete todo list.

Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Used with limit to control pagination. For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns todos 1-20, page=2 returns todos 21-40.

limit.description:
Number of todo items to return per page. Controls the page size for pagination results.

Must be between 1 and 100 to balance performance and usability. Smaller values reduce response size, larger values reduce request count. Default value of 20 is recommended for typical todo list views.

search.description:
Search term for partial matching across todo title and description fields. Enables users to find todos by typing keywords.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching on both title and description columns. For example, searching 'meeting' would match 'Team Meeting', 'Prepare meeting notes', and todos with 'meeting' in their description.

status.description:
Filter todos by lifecycle status. Allows users to view todos in a specific workflow state.

Supported values:
- 'pending': Not yet started tasks
- 'in_progress': Tasks actively being worked on
- 'completed': Finished tasks
- 'cancelled': Abandoned tasks

When specified, returns only todos with the matching status. When null or omitted, returns todos of all statuses.

completed.description:
Filter todos by completion status. Controls whether to show completed todos, incomplete todos, or all todos.

When true, returns only completed todos. When false, returns only incomplete/pending todos. When null or omitted, returns all todos regardless of completion status.

priority.description:
Filter todos by priority level. Allows users to view todos of a specific priority.

Supported values: 'low', 'medium', 'high'. When specified, returns only todos with the matching priority level. When null or omitted, returns todos of all priority levels.

due_after.description:
Filter todos with due dates after this timestamp. Enables querying todos due in the future or within a specific timeframe.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z'). Used with due_before to define date ranges for due date filtering.

due_before.description:
Filter todos with due dates before this timestamp. Enables querying overdue todos or todos due within a specific timeframe.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). Used with due_after to define date ranges for due date filtering.

order_by.description:
Field to sort the todo list by. Determines the ordering criteria for returned todo results.

Supported values: 'created_at' (creation date), 'due_date' (due date), 'priority' (priority level), 'completed' (completion status), 'title' (alphabetical). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the order_by field. Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order.

'asc' for ascending order (oldest first for dates, A-Z for text, low to high for priority). 'desc' for descending order (newest first for dates, Z-A for text, high to low for priority).

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, and sorting the authenticated user's todo list with pagination support. Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for efficient todo management.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters with configurable page sizes. Enables flexible searching through general search term that queries both title and description. Allows filtering by completion status, priority level, and due date ranges. Provides sorting options by multiple fields including creation date, due date, priority, completion status, and alphabetical title order.

All filter parameters are optional and can be combined for complex queries. For example, users can search for incomplete high-priority todos due this week. The filters work together to narrow results progressively. Date range filters can be used to find overdue tasks (due_before=now) or upcoming tasks (due_after=now).

This request type is scoped to the authenticated user - all queries automatically filter to only the requesting user's todos through the user_id extracted from the JWT token, ensuring data privacy and ownership controls.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo item.

This UUID v4 string uniquely identifies the todo item and is used for referencing the task in detail views and update operations.

title.description:
The title or name of the todo item.

This field provides the primary task description displayed in list views. It concisely identifies the task for quick scanning and selection.

description.description:
Optional detailed description providing additional context for the todo item.

This field contains extended notes, instructions, or context about the task. It provides additional information beyond the title, helping users understand task requirements and details when reviewing their todo lists. Can be null if the title is self-explanatory.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the todo item.

Indicates the task's workflow state for filtering and organization in list views:
- 'pending': Not yet started
- 'in_progress': Actively being worked on
- 'completed': Finished
- 'cancelled': Abandoned

priority.description:
Priority level of the todo item.

Displays task importance for sorting and visual highlighting in list views:
- 'low': Can wait
- 'medium': Standard priority
- 'high': Urgent
- null: No priority assigned

due_date.description:
Due date and time for the todo item.

Shows the task deadline in list views for identifying upcoming or overdue tasks. Displayed in ISO 8601 format or null if no deadline is set.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

Boolean flag indicating whether the task is complete (true) or incomplete (false). Used for filtering between active and completed task lists.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was marked as completed.

Records the exact date and time when the user completed this task. This field is automatically set when the todo status changes to completed and is cleared when a todo is marked incomplete. Displayed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Null for incomplete todos.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was created.

Shows task age in list views and enables chronological sorting. Displayed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the todo item.

Records when any field of the todo was last changed, enabling users to identify recently modified tasks in their list views. Updated automatically by the system whenever the todo is modified. Displayed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item optimized for list views and search results.

This lightweight schema provides essential information for displaying todos in lists without the overhead of complete details. It includes the core identifying and organizational fields needed for task lists while excluding verbose content like full descriptions and less critical metadata.

The summary DTO is ideal for:
- Todo list displays showing multiple items
- Search result previews
- Dashboard widgets and summaries
- Mobile applications with limited screen space

Users can access full details by requesting the complete ITodoListTodo representation for specific items they want to view or edit in detail.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo item.

This is a UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies each todo item in the system. The ID is automatically generated upon creation and remains immutable throughout the item's lifecycle.

This identifier is used in API operations to reference specific todo items for retrieval, updates, and deletion.

title.description:
The title or name of the todo item.

This field represents the main text description of the task. It provides a concise summary that identifies the task at a glance and serves as the primary display text in todo lists.

The title is required and must be between 1 and 200 characters to ensure readability while providing sufficient detail.

description.description:
Optional detailed description or notes about the todo item.

This field provides space for additional context, instructions, or comprehensive information related to the task. Users can include step-by-step instructions, links, background context, or any other details that don't fit in the title.

The description supports up to 2000 characters to accommodate detailed task documentation while maintaining reasonable storage limits. This field is optional and may be null if no additional details are provided.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the todo item.

This field tracks the todo's workflow state through its lifecycle. Valid values represent different stages of task progression:
- 'pending': Initial state when the todo is created but not yet started
- 'in_progress': Task is actively being worked on
- 'completed': Task has been finished successfully
- 'cancelled': Task has been abandoned or is no longer relevant

The status field provides more granular workflow tracking compared to the boolean completed flag, enabling users to distinguish between tasks that are actively being worked on versus those that are simply not finished. This field is required and must always have one of the defined values.

priority.description:
Priority level of the todo item.

This field indicates the importance or urgency of the task using a three-tier classification system:
- 'low': Tasks that can be completed when time permits
- 'medium': Standard priority tasks
- 'high': Urgent or important tasks requiring immediate attention

The priority helps users organize their workload and focus on the most critical tasks first. This field is optional and may be null.

due_date.description:
Due date and time for the todo item.

This field specifies the deadline by which the task should be completed. The value is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) to support precise deadline tracking across different time zones.

This field is optional and may be null for tasks without specific deadlines. When set, it enables deadline-based sorting, filtering, and overdue notifications.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

This boolean field indicates whether the task has been marked as complete (true) or is still pending/in-progress (false).

The completion status is central to task management workflows, affecting how items are displayed in filtered views and contributing to productivity statistics and completion rate calculations.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the todo was marked as completed.

This field captures the exact date and time when the task's status changed to completed. The value is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format and is automatically set by the system when the user marks the todo as complete.

The field is automatically cleared (set to null) if the todo is subsequently marked as incomplete. For todos that have never been completed or are currently incomplete, this field is null. This timestamp enables completion time analytics and provides historical tracking of when tasks were actually finished.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was created.

This field records the exact date and time when the todo item was first added to the system. The value is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format and is automatically set by the system upon creation.

This timestamp is immutable and provides historical context for task age and creation patterns.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.

This field records the most recent modification time for the todo item. The value is automatically updated by the system whenever any field of the todo is modified.

This timestamp helps users track when tasks were last changed and supports audit trails for task modifications.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the todo was deleted.

This field supports soft deletion functionality, recording the exact date and time when the todo item was marked as deleted. When this field is null, the todo is active and visible in normal queries. When set to a timestamp, the todo is considered deleted and excluded from standard list operations while being preserved in the database.

Soft deletion enables data recovery and maintains audit trails without permanently removing task data. Users typically don't see deleted todos in their active lists, but administrators or recovery processes can access them if needed. This field is automatically set by the system when a delete operation is performed.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Complete representation of a todo item entity.

This schema represents the full structure of a todo item as stored in the todo_list_todos table and returned by API operations. It contains all properties of a task including identification, content, metadata, and timestamps.

Each todo item belongs to a specific authenticated user (referenced by user_id in the database, but excluded from this DTO as it comes from authentication context). The system enforces strict ownership rules ensuring users can only access and manipulate their own todo items.

This complete representation is returned from operations like create, update, and retrieve individual todos. It includes system-managed fields like id, created_at, and updated_at that are not modifiable through update operations.

The entity supports core task management features including title, optional description, priority levels, due dates, and completion tracking.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new todo item.

This schema defines the data required from clients when creating a new todo through the POST /todos endpoint. It includes only the fields that users can specify during todo creation, excluding system-managed fields like id, user_id, and timestamps.

The user_id is automatically populated from the authenticated user's JWT token, ensuring todos are created under the correct user account. The id and timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are generated by the system upon creation.

Clients should provide at minimum the required title field. Optional fields (description, status, priority, due_date, completed) allow users to fully configure their todo at creation time, though they can be updated later through the PUT endpoint.

Default values: status defaults to 'pending', priority defaults to 'medium', completed defaults to false if not specified.

title.description:
Brief summary or name of the todo item being created.

This required field serves as the primary identifier for the todo. It must be a non-empty string between 1 and 200 characters that concisely describes the task. The length constraint ensures titles remain suitable for optimal display in list views while providing sufficient space for meaningful task descriptions.

Examples: "Complete project report", "Buy groceries", "Schedule dentist appointment"

description.description:
Detailed information about the todo item.

This optional field allows users to provide extended notes, context, or instructions for the task. It can contain multiple paragraphs, subtasks, links, or any other relevant details that don't fit in the title. The field supports up to 2000 characters to accommodate comprehensive task documentation while maintaining reasonable storage limits.

If omitted or set to null, the todo will rely solely on its title. Users can add or modify the description later through the update endpoint.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status for the todo item.

This optional field allows users to set the starting workflow state when creating the todo:
- 'pending': Task is created but not yet started (default if not specified)
- 'in_progress': Task is being actively worked on from creation
- 'completed': Task is already complete (useful for logging finished work)
- 'cancelled': Task is created but immediately marked as no longer relevant

Most todos are created with status='pending' or by omitting this field (which defaults to 'pending'). Users can change the status later through the update endpoint as work progresses.

priority.description:
Priority level indicating the importance or urgency of the todo item.

This optional field allows users to categorize their task by priority:
- 'low': Non-urgent tasks that can be done when time permits
- 'medium': Standard priority for typical tasks (default if not specified)
- 'high': Important or urgent tasks requiring prompt attention
- null: No priority assigned

If not provided during creation, the system defaults to 'medium' priority. Users can change the priority later as task urgency changes.

due_date.description:
Target completion date and time for the todo item.

This optional field lets users set a deadline for their task. When provided, it must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). The due date helps with planning and identifying approaching or overdue tasks.

If omitted or set to null, the todo has no specific deadline and can be completed at any time. Users can add or modify the due date later as plans change.

completed.description:
Initial completion status for the todo item.

This optional field allows users to set the completion state when creating the todo:
- false: Task is incomplete and pending (default if not specified)
- true: Task is marked as already completed (useful when logging already-finished tasks)

Most todos are created with completed=false or omitting this field (which defaults to false). Users can toggle completion status later through the update endpoint.

title.description:
The title or name of the todo item.

This field represents the main text description of the task. It should be concise yet descriptive enough to identify the task at a glance. The title is the primary display text shown in todo lists and serves as the main identifier for the task.

Validation constraints ensure the title is between 1 and 200 characters to maintain readability while allowing sufficient detail.

description.description:
Optional detailed description or notes about the todo item.

This field provides space for additional context, instructions, or notes related to the task. Users can include more comprehensive information that doesn't fit in the title, such as step-by-step instructions, links, or background context. The field supports up to 2000 characters to accommodate detailed task documentation.

The description is optional and can be null if no additional details are needed.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the todo item.

This field tracks the todo's workflow state through its lifecycle. The status indicates where the task currently stands in the completion process and helps users organize their work by progress stage.

Valid status values:
- 'pending': Initial state when the todo is created but not yet started
- 'in_progress': The task is actively being worked on
- 'completed': The task has been finished
- 'cancelled': The task has been abandoned or is no longer relevant

Updating the status field allows users to track their workflow and progress. The status works in conjunction with the completed boolean field to provide comprehensive task state tracking.

priority.description:
Priority level of the todo item.

This field indicates the importance or urgency of the task, helping users organize and prioritize their workload. The priority system uses three levels:
- 'low': Tasks that can be completed when time permits
- 'medium': Standard priority tasks
- 'high': Urgent or important tasks requiring immediate attention

The priority field is optional and can be null if no priority classification is assigned.

due_date.description:
Due date and time for the todo item.

This field specifies when the task should be completed. The value is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) to support precise deadline tracking across different time zones.

The due date is optional and can be null for tasks without specific deadlines. When set, it helps users manage time-sensitive tasks and enables features like overdue notifications or deadline-based sorting.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

This field indicates whether the task has been completed or is still pending. Setting this to true marks the task as done, while false indicates the task is incomplete or in progress.

Updating this field is the primary mechanism for tracking task completion. The completion status affects how the item is displayed in filtered views (e.g., completed vs. pending lists) and contributes to productivity statistics.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the todo was marked as completed.

This field allows users to manually set or update the completion timestamp for a todo item. While the system typically sets this automatically when a task is marked complete, users may need to update it to correct the completion time, backdate a completion, or clear it when marking a task as incomplete again.

The value should be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). Setting this field to null clears the completion timestamp, which is appropriate when marking a previously completed task as incomplete or in-progress.

This field works in conjunction with the completed boolean field to provide comprehensive completion tracking. When updating completed to true, users may also set completed_at to record the exact completion time. When setting completed to false, users typically set completed_at to null to indicate the task is no longer finished.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing todo item.

This schema defines the structure for partial updates to todo items in the authenticated user's task list. All fields are optional, allowing users to update only specific properties while leaving others unchanged. The system applies only the provided fields to the existing todo item, preserving any omitted fields at their current values.

Security: Updates are restricted to the authenticated user's own todo items. The system automatically validates ownership by comparing the todo's user_id with the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system upon successful update and should not be included in this request schema.

This DTO is used exclusively for PUT /todoList/user/todos/{todoId} operations where users modify their existing tasks.

total_count.description:
Total number of todo items created by the user.

This metric represents the complete count of all todo items in the user's collection, regardless of completion status. It includes both completed and pending tasks, providing a measure of overall task volume.

This count is computed by executing a COUNT(*) query on the todo_list_todos table filtered by the authenticated user's ID.

completed_count.description:
Number of todo items marked as completed.

This metric counts all tasks where the 'completed' field is set to true, indicating tasks that have been finished. It provides insight into user productivity and task completion behavior.

This count is computed using COUNT(*) with a WHERE clause filtering for completed=true and the authenticated user's ID.

pending_count.description:
Number of todo items that are not yet completed.

This metric counts all tasks where the 'completed' field is set to false, representing active or in-progress tasks. It helps users understand their current workload and outstanding responsibilities.

This count is computed using COUNT(*) with a WHERE clause filtering for completed=false and the authenticated user's ID.

completion_rate.description:
Percentage of completed todos out of total todos.

This calculated metric represents the user's task completion rate as a percentage value between 0 and 100. It is computed as (completed_count / total_count) * 100, providing a measure of productivity and task management effectiveness.

When total_count is zero, this value is 0. The rate helps users track their overall completion performance and identify productivity trends.

ITodoListTodoStatistics.description:
Statistical metrics and aggregated data about a user's todo items.

This schema represents computed analytics derived from the user's todo collection in the todo_list_todos table. Unlike entity DTOs that map directly to database rows, this is a statistical summary generated through aggregation queries (COUNT, SUM, AVG operations).

The statistics provide users with dashboard-style insights into their task management patterns including completion rates, pending workload, and overall productivity metrics. All metrics are automatically filtered to include only the authenticated user's data, ensuring complete privacy and data isolation.

This DTO is returned by the GET /todoList/user/todos/statistics operation and serves analytical and reporting requirements. The metrics are computed in real-time to reflect the current state of the user's todo collection.

Use cases include productivity dashboards, overview screens, progress tracking, and user engagement metrics.
